07

Outstanding work the programme does not measure

From the Rev02 appendix registers at the data date. None of this carries schedule units, so none of it appears in the 4.19 percent the programme still shows as remaining.

Where the Contractor's own files disagree with each other

Each row is two numbers for the same thing, both taken from the Rev02 package. Settle the denominator before either number is quoted in correspondence, and never mix the two in one sentence.

ARecorded is not accepted

The programme records an actual date when the Contractor enters one. That is a record of an event, not ASCE's acceptance of it. A milestone marked complete, an ECC marked signed and a system marked handed over are three different gates, and only the last carries acceptance. Nothing on this page, at any percentage, should be reported to AUC as accepted completion.

BA forecast date that has passed is a request, not a result

The programme was recalculated on 25 August 2026. Every activity dated before today and still open is a date the Contractor has already missed, not a delay ASCE has agreed. Treat it as an update request to the Contractor, and record the reply with its evidence reference in the change log in section 05.

08

HCIS approvals

High Commission for Industrial Security. Five separate risks in Appendix 12 carry the same cause, it is the largest single open system in the procurement register, and both HCIS permits are still open on the permits register. Everything below is counted live from the programme and the registers.

The permits themselves

Source: Appendix 6, sheet Permits Register, lines 10 and 11. That sheet's status column was last refreshed on 18 March 2025, so treat the wording as the last recorded position and confirm it with the Contractor before it is used in correspondence. The live Permits sheet in the same file carries no HCIS line at all, which is itself worth closing out.

Risks with HCIS as the cause

Source: Appendix 12 Risk Register. All five score 20, Very High. None carries an owner, an action owner, a treatment strategy or a risk action date.

Procurement waiting on the HCIS chain

Source: Appendix 8 Procurement Register, sheet Task Tracker-new. HCIS is 12 of the 32 open lines, more than any other system. Required at site dates are the Contractor's own.

Programme activities in the HCIS chain

Every activity in the Rev02 programme whose name, facility or activity ID carries HCIS. Open section 05 and press the HCIS button to see the same set in the live dashboard, broken down by discipline, system, sub system, zone, facility and month.

09

ECC and MCC certificates

Both handover logs in one register, tied to the programme. The Power package log at 20 August and the Water package log at 3 September. An ECC is the construction completion certificate for one system in one building; it has to be submitted, walked down, cleared of Category A punch items and signed before that system can go into an MCC and be handed over.

By package

By zone and sub system

By discipline

By area

How this ties to the activities. Every ECC carries the zone and sub system it belongs to, so it is linked to the programme in every case. Where the log names a building the programme also names, the ECC is pinned to that facility and the table shows that facility's live activity completion beside it. Press Activities on any row to open section 05 at that facility. Counts here are ECC packages, not activities.

Denominators. The Power log's own ECC Summary reads 597 anticipated and 527 signed; its detail sheets carry 659 rows of which 523 are signed. The Water log's dashboard reads 528 anticipated across the five areas; its detail sheets carry 576 rows. Both gaps are in the Contractor's own file, between summary and detail. Reconcile them before either number is used in correspondence.

10

Outstanding works register

The ASCE register of what is still open against the Contractor, in four groups. Each NCR is looked up in Appendix 15 and each Power package in the Appendix 11 MCC list, so the status shown is the register's own, not a typed in one.

Where each status comes from. NCR status, raised date and closed date are read from Appendix 15, NCR Status August 2026. The Power packages are matched to the Appendix 11 MCC list by area and sequence number, and the date shown is the ECC/MCC received date. Engineering deviations and O&M obligations carry no register status, so they read as open with ASCE until one is recorded.

Update the data

Two ways to keep this page current. Drop a file in and the page updates itself for the whole team. Once a month, when a new programme is issued, the page is rebuilt from the files listed underneath.

Drop a file in

Reads .xlsx, .csv and a paste straight out of Excel. Nothing is changed until you have seen the table and pressed apply. Every change carries your name and goes in the change log.

Columns it looks for:
Drop the file here, or click to choose one Appendix 1(A), Appendix 15, the ECC log, or any sheet saved as .csv
Or paste the rows out of Excel

What to send for the full monthly rebuild

A new programme changes every figure on this page, so it is rebuilt rather than patched. Send the whole Rev folder. These are the files that are actually read, and what each one drives.
